## The principle for the batches

Every batch lands with the specification, the library and both paths agreeing. So the work is grouped by what has to change together, not split finer.

Two rules of the batch machinery shape the order: two rungs in one batch may not change the same declaration, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, since every rung branches from the batch's base (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:465`, batch rule 1). That is why the wrapping operators and the flattening sit in different batches, and why rung O's check follows the operators.

How a phase-3 batch's content is chosen (the coordinator's method, as batch 10 was planned): the measure is the distance, the compiled checker's errors on the one library, and the source is the last landed gate's per-site list (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), every error with its site and class. The planner, an Opus worker, sorts it into three piles: (1) decided and free to fix, the library's one-off slips and the checker's defects with a known fix, which go into the batch; (2) waiting on a decision of Pavol's or a judgement (after batch 9: the arrays, 98, after the switch-over by his answer to batch 8's Q4; the self-typed bodies, 30, a list of ways and a judgement first; `isLeftZero` and items 37 to 42, his), which are held and listed in the record; (3) waiting on a probe, which is probed before the record is written (P1 for row 424's F-bounded half). Pile 1 gains the defects the last review routed as owed, the items this plan queues ("a checker rung after batch 8"), and his decisions ready to build (item 20). The pile is cut into rungs by code area, no two rungs on one declaration and none building on another (the two rules above), usually four, since one landing pays for them all and the harness runs two agents at once. Fable reviews the record in place; a question goes to Pavol only where a pile-2 item needs his word. There is no target size and no target cost per error: the planner takes what of pile 1 fits the rungs (batch 10: 148 of the 340, 192 held).

## Part 3. Skill sentences the batch made false

For the skill writer. The gather's record gives the revival changes of both rungs and finds no skill sentence false by either (`RECORD.md`, "Revival changes, for the skill writer"); the writer's task 20 and its cold read took them (`0cf48c7b2`, `df58b05b8`), and the coordinator's two commit rules with the check-in file and the landing's sweep (`1130effc7`, `222c9d5fe`). Lines below are of `.claude/skills/` at `066725e0a`.

**Made false by batch 20, beyond those:** none found. I read the parts that the two rungs' subjects reach: `fortress-repo`'s `SKILL.md` on numbers, `library.md`, `interpreter.md`, `compiler.md`, `gate.md`, `committing.md`, `records.md`, `tests-writing.md` and `revival-changes.md` whole on numbers, arrays, sizes and abstract methods; `coordinator`'s `SKILL.md`, `batch.md` and `delegating.md` on check-ins, commits and the landing; `cloud-container`'s `stops.md`.

**Not false, but incomplete or stale, each met by this batch:**
- **`fortress-repo/references/records.md:56`**, "A row at its 1,200-character limit takes no further note.": `ledger.py` also refuses a note that takes a row's notes past 700 characters (`explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py:22-23`, `:115`). Row 441 stood at 702 of 700 and row 465 at 673; skeptic A counted row 465's room against 1,200 alone, and five notes were refused (`RECORD.md:128-137`). Add the notes' limit to the sentence.
- **`fortress-repo/references/interpreter.md:84`**, the quick pair "in about 56 s for both": at batches 19 and 20 the pair took 44 s and 47 s at once. Approximate, not false.
- **`fortress-repo/references/gate.md:3`**, "in about 25 minutes": 20.4 and 21.7 minutes at the last two gates. Approximate, not false.
- **P-79 has no worker-facing sentence.** A rung that breaks a team demo now rewrites it in the same batch where the way is known (`POSITIONS.md:85`), but no part of `fortress-repo` says that no suite runs the demos or how a rung checks one; `tests-running.md`, "Outside the gate" (`:54-57`), names `not_passing_yet/` and seven unrun folders, and not `ProjectFortress/demos/`. Briefs quote POSITIONS, so nothing is false; a line there would let a rung find the demos it touches.

**Rules the batch broke that stay true:** `cloud-container/references/stops.md:59` and `coordinator/references/delegating.md:44` on arming check-ins in one turn; `fortress-repo/references/committing.md:20-28` on one command per commit and on saying that a commit edits the original tree (section 6). **Checked and not false:** `revival-changes.md`'s new sections "An integer power", "The rational power over any integer" and "The result types of vectors and matrices, and the api's array declarations"; its "Arithmetic in a size" (a size's power at a negative exponent stays refused), "Overflow", "`fill` and `tabulate`" and "Vectors and matrices at an element type that is not a number type"; `library.md:23` and `:26`; `compiler.md:125`'s "about a minute" (63 s); `batch.md:45` (4 of 4 briefed agents read it, none in the first turn).

- **I.worker.1 and I.skeptic.1** (`IntegerDivisionByZero`, row 792): `PLAN.md:526`, "Default: `DivisionByZero`". Sound.
- **I.worker.2 and I.skeptic.2** (the demos' timing line, row 791): a sentence in the demos' entry (`PLAN.md:232`), "Default: as they are". **Settled by P-79** since about 11:50 UTC: "`BiCGSTAB`'s timing line (row 791)" is among the demos to respell. # Climb batch 20: the gather's record

Written at the gather stage of climb batch 20 (2026-10-20), the run of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-20.md` (rungs I and A), on `main` from the base `97ccd5f1f9f8ae69c2c9ff4f3dfca7c7fd102059`. `main` was at `56d084018` when the gather began, five coordinator commits above the base that touch only `explorations/coordinator/BOOT.md`, `HELD.md`, `INDEX.md`, `review-queue.md`, `process-engineering/task-list-archaeology.md` and `tools/sweep-tasks.py` (`git diff --name-only 97ccd5f1f 56d084018`), no file a rung touches. Both rungs were approved by their skeptics, with no contested fix, no judge and no repair round. No branch is a parent of anything on `main`, and each branch stays as it is.

**Preconditions.** `git status --porcelain` printed nothing, and `97ccd5f1f` is an ancestor of `HEAD` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, exit 0).

**Scratch.** The patches are `tmp/gather/<slug>.patch` in the main tree, each `git diff 97ccd5f1f...<branch>`. One tree was seeded outside the main tree from the batch's base build, with `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base20 /home/user/fortress-gather20 - 97ccd5f1f9f8ae69c2c9ff4f3dfca7c7fd102059` ("seeded from /home/user/fortress-base20 (97ccd5f1f) in 4 s"); nothing was built or run in the main tree or in the base build. In `/home/user/fortress-gather20` the two patches were applied in the order below with `git apply --3way --index` (no conflict), then `ant compileAll` ("Caches /home/user/fortress-gather20/default_repository/caches started again, empty", "BUILD SUCCESSFUL", "Total time: 49 seconds") and the library order (five compiles, each `rc=0`, five jars in `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`). The closing tests and the interaction check ran there. `diff <(git diff 97ccd5f1f HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml Specification) <(git -C /home/user/fortress-gather20 diff --cached 97ccd5f1f -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml Specification)`, run on `main` at `408910f26`, printed nothing: the code, tests and specification the tests ran on are `main`'s.

## The landed commits

| Order | Rung | Branch | Commit on `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | I, `rung-integer-power` | `wip/rung-integer-power` at `981fd6fef` | `5ad4a9957` |
| 2 | A, `rung-array-sites` | `wip/rung-array-sites` at `f3858cf85` | `e487cec2d` (its net change), `444f37018` (its record and message) |
| | the rows' closes | | `408910f26` |

No rung declares `landsOnlyWith`, so the first rule orders nothing.

**Rung A's change is in a commit the gather did not write.** The gather applied rung A's patch with `git apply --3way --index` to `main`'s index after committing rung I, and before it folded A's record the coordinating session committed its boot note, `e487cec2d` ("Boot note: the next check-in", 08:41 UTC), with a commit that took the whole index: `git show --stat e487cec2d` lists rung A's `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, its three test files, its `REPORT.md`, `SKEPTIC.md` and `record.md`, beside `explorations/coordinator/BOOT.md`. It was pushed to `origin/main` with `5ad4a9957` (`git branch -r --contains e487cec2d`: `origin/main`, `origin/claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8`, `origin/blinded-fable`). Rewriting it would need a force-push of `main`, which cannot be undone and which the gather did not take (gather.3, below). So rung A's code and tests are `e487cec2d`'s, exactly the branch's net change on rung I's commit (`git diff --stat 5ad4a9957 e487cec2d` lists the eight files of rung A's patch and `BOOT.md`; `git diff e487cec2d 408910f26 -- Library ProjectFortress Specification` prints nothing), and `444f37018` carries the rung's title, its message with the reason, its record's fold, the placeholders numbered and `record.md` taken out again. Row 678 is closed by `e487cec2d`, the commit that holds its fix. The gather's two later commits, the closes and this record, each staged and committed in one command, so that no other commit could take their paths.

## The order the rungs were applied in

I, then A: the manifest's order, and the order of the lowest edited lines. The two rungs share two files, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` (`comm -12` of the two lists `git diff --name-only 97ccd5f1f...<branch>`). In each, I's lowest edited line comes first: `FortressLibrary.fss` I `:642` (`QQ`'s power), A `:2524` (`Vector`'s `fill`); `FortressLibrary.fsi` I `:283` (`MultiplicativeRing`'s power), A `:1499` (`immutableArray`), from `git diff -U0 97ccd5f1f...<branch>`'s hunk headers. - P-153 **An integer raised to a negative power raises an error; a fraction comes from a float or rational base (contract E, item 58).** Each integer type's `^` answers its own type at every exponent: a negative exponent raises `IntegerOverflow` where the result is no integer, a base of 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power. A program that wants a fraction writes a float or rational base, as `2.0^(-1)`. Why: the team's later code types an integer power by its integer at a signed exponent (P-26); overloads choose by type, and no type carries an exponent's or a numeral's sign, so the split is on the base, with the sign tested at run time as the library tests every sign-refined subset (P-80). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes

## 2. The forks, with their defaults

**Consequential** means what the `coordinator` skill's `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", gives: it reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of yours; it touches microGPT's lines, speed or readability; it chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent; or it cannot be undone. Each fork below is marked. Each default can be undone, and none reverses a decision of yours.

### Forks the batch takes, none consequential

1. **The batch's scope: rungs I and A.** Default: as section 1 gives it. Not consequential: a choice of what is ready, by PLAN's method (the distance's decided sites first) and the planner's probe, reversible in the next batch.
2. **The arrays and decision E's diff: one rung, A.** Default: one rung (section 1). Not consequential: how the work is cut, settled by P-40's "built with the array sites' other fixes" and by the first export error, which clears only with both patches.
3. **The integer power: its own rung, I.** Default: its own rung (section 1). Not consequential: two decisions, two areas, no shared declaration, and the three patches measured applying together.
4. **The array ways as `ways.patch` has them:** the leaf `fill` and `tabulate` for 5 bodies and the `cast` for 9 (1a with 1c), the `cast` in the factory arms (2a), the `cast` of the subscript's value for `Col` and `Row` (3d). Default: as the patch. Not consequential: each is in the ways note's column of ways that need no decision (`reviews/array-sites-ways.md`, section 5), the library's own devices by P-27: a leaf redeclares a parent's method at its own type as `Array1`, `Array2` and `ImmutableArray1` redeclare `copy`, `map`, `ivmap` and `replica`, and the library's `cast` gives a factory's result its sized type, as `array1` and `array2` already do (row 685). The ways not taken, such as 1c alone and 3a's `SubArray2`, are the note's, and the rung's section names those it leaves.
5. **The api's `immutableArray` ranks 2 and 3 put in a comment** (the probe's 4d; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1500-1501`). The component has had them in a comment since the team's last commit (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2264-2280`; `a874948ac`), and the library has no `ImmutableArray2` or `ImmutableArray3`, so no program can call them. They leave the library chapter of the specification, Part IV, which is the api rendered (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27-37`). Default: as the patch; a point to report, on your review list. Not consequential: the library splits with itself, and the built side wins by the library's own standard, as for `FlatString`'s pair in climb batch 19 (`reviews/batch-19-review.md`, Part 1, split 2); the lines come back by removing the comment.
6. **A guard test of the casts at all eight element types the bound admits.** The ways note measured the casts under walk at four types and the transposed matrix (its section 6, M1), and the other four by reading. Default: A writes a walk test that asserts every cast body's value at `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64`; it passes on the base and after. Not consequential: a cast that fails raises `CastError` where the base answered a value, and the guard shows none does.
7. **`MultiplicativeRing`'s `^` in the api.** The api writes `opr ^(self, other:ZZ64): T`, the component `opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral): T` with no body (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:283`, `.fss:377`). Three texts, each measured with rung A's patches beside (section 4): (a) `abstract opr ^(self, other:AnyIntegral): T` alone brings a new site, 'The inherited abstract method ^ ... from the trait MultiplicativeRing[\RR64\] has no concrete implementation in the object FloatLiteral in component FortressBuiltin', since `RR64`'s api lacks the component's `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64` (`.fss:486-487`, under the team's comment "Shouldn't need this extra declaration."); (b) the exponent alone, `AnyIntegral`, leaves the entry, which then differs, by reading, only in `abstract`; (c) `abstract` and `AnyIntegral`, with `RR64`'s api declaring the component's `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64`: the entry gone, nothing come. Default: (c). Not consequential: the brief puts this entry with P-153; `abstract` is how the same api trait writes its other bodiless members, `one` and `TIMES` (`.fsi:279-280`); and an api that states its component's declaration is the library's own way.
8. **`QQ`'s api exponent `AnyIntegral`** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:430`, row 445's api half). Default: in rung I. Not consequential: the row's own fix, the type the component and the specification give.
9. **`QQ`'s body: the `typecase` of the probe's section 4**, the library's device for "any integer" (`exactValue`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:398-408`). Default: as probed, in `power.patch`. Not consequential: P-153's build, as the Fable judgement's section 6 gives it.
10. **`IntLiteral`'s `^` answers `IntLiteral`** (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:552-554`, `.fsi:213-214`), as the probe wrote E. Default: as probed. Not consequential: P-153's "each integer type's `^` answers its own type", applied to the numeral's type (P-76); under walk a numeral is a `ZZ32` value and reaches it once in the suite (the probe, section 1.1).
11. **Row 445's walk half, part (1): the six power natives read the exponent with `getLong`, which a `ZZ` value always refuses** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FBigNum.java:48-50`). Each native's reader is its own (`Int.java:223`, `Long.java:235`, `NN32.java:230`, `UnsignedLong.java:230`, `BigNum.java:110-116`, `IntLiteral.java:107-113`, each used by `Pow` alone). After rung I, the specification gives E and walk builds it, but the compiled path's own library still answers 0, and a raw exception at 0, through `jIntExp` (row 523), until phase 4's natives. The planner's Java check: `1.0/10^k` and `Math.pow(10.0, -k)` are one double at k = 1, 2, 4 and 16, and so are the products the tests assert and print (section 4); the rung sees the respelled tests pass on the base before its edit, and where a respelled line does not keep its value or its parse there (`compoundArray` tests array literals written with juxtaposition), it writes the scale another way that keeps them and says so. Default: so respelled; `simpleExp`'s comment, "that Int and Long exponentiation work (largely) as expected", kept, since the rung's own test now checks the integer bases. Not consequential: P-153 names them; a point to report, each line with its before and after.

### Points the batch lists for you, not questions

- **Team lines changed:** every integer `^` declaration of the api and the component (the team's of 2008, beside the revival's numeral overloads of 2026-10-02) and `QQ`'s body (Guy Steele's, 2008); `MultiplicativeRing`'s and `QQ`'s api powers; walk's six power natives; `strToInt`'s `fail`; the team tests `realArith`, `compoundArray` and `simpleExp` (2007) and the demos `BiCGSTAB`, `BiCGSTAB2` and `npbft` (I). - P-153 **An integer raised to a negative power raises an error; a fraction comes from a float or rational base (contract E, item 58).** Each integer type's `^` answers its own type at every exponent: a negative exponent raises `IntegerOverflow` where the result is no integer, a base of 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power. A program that wants a fraction writes a float or rational base, as `2.0^(-1)`. Why: the team's later code types an integer power by its integer at a signed exponent (P-26); overloads choose by type, and no type carries an exponent's or a numeral's sign, so the split is on the base, with the sign tested at run time as the library tests every sign-refined subset (P-80). Still to build: the integer powers so typed, with row 747's typed `fail` in `strToInt`, and the team tests `realArith`, `compoundArray` and `simpleExp` and two demos written with a float base (PLAN item 58).
- P-40 **Sizes are checked, and a size left unknown is an error only where it is used.** The checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters and refuses a size beyond `NN32` or `ZZ32` (F-140). Storage refuses a JVM array length over 2^31-1. A size that inference leaves unknown is an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value. How the checker represents it is not his choice. A size that a call cannot fix refuses the call, also inside an overload set, instead of dropping the arm (row 400, its compiled half open). Every static argument but an operator counts in the exclusion rule; booleans join once the checker has boolean parameters (row 406). A size used as a value converts to `ZZ32` as a numeral does (row 485). The unused sizes of the api's 17 vector and matrix operators go by decision E's diff, which he read and took for the switch-over (ask 3, 2026-10-20; `perf-probes/array-sites/e3-rebased.patch`): it finishes the team's own fix of 2008, which took them out of the component only (F-35), and is built with the array sites' other fixes. The other unused sizes of the 25 go only by a diff shown to him.
- P-79 **Every team demo is kept running as the tree changes (2026-10-20).** A demo that a change breaks is rewritten in the same batch where the way is known, as climb batch 20's rung I wrote `10.0^(-6)` in three demos; one that fails for want of a feature runs again once the feature is built. His word of 2026-10-20 replaces his earlier "Let's not touch them", which likely came when a fix needed a feature not yet built. So the demos that fail today are respelled where the way is known: the five refused at load (row 670), `trips.fss` (row 710), `BiCGSTAB`'s timing line (row 791), and the static arguments a reduction needs under P-48 (row 731). Still to build: a measurement of which demos run, and a rung for those with a known way.
- F-35 **The `FortressLibrary` api has 8 declarations with a dead size, a size parameter that occurs in no parameter type, return type or body.** It had 25 until climb batch 20's rung A took the sizes out of the 17 vector and matrix operators by decision E's diff (P-40; F-264). They check clean (P-40). They stand in the oldest library in the history, of 2007-01-04 (`72ae6881b`), where the six vector forms, scalar ones included, carry the matrix product's `nat n, nat m, nat p` beside it, with no `where` clause; in 2008 Jan-Willem Maessen took them out of the component while fixing walk's unification ("tons of latent type bugs came out", `32153798d`), and the api kept them. Where the component omits the dead size, the export checker reports the api's declaration missing. Six vector `DOT` and juxtaposition operators had this shape, `[\T, nat n, nat m, nat p\]` in the api and `[\T, nat n\]` in the component, and gave one of the distance's export errors, gone since (F-264). P-40 lets the other dead sizes go only by a diff shown to the curator. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 7.
- F-54 **The gate classes the distance to the switch-over by root cause.** The `#class` rows of each gate's `distance.txt` hold the counts. At climb batch 19's gate the sized arrays (class V2, 17 of 31) and the one-off body errors (class OT, 9) led; climb batch 20's rung A took class V2 to 0 on its tree (F-264). No coercion into an arbitrary `I extends Integral[\I\]` can be declared, so a numeral where such an `I` is expected needs `x.zero` or `x.one`. Row 680's crash hid no error: with its repair (F-233) the component's check finds none in `Array3`, and the distance lost its crash row. With `StandardMinMax[\T\]` added to the array bound, the overloading check ran past 15 minutes when measured, before row 688's memo. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md` sections 2 and 3.4; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` section 6.

**Subscripts (124): a design choice.**
- **The team's own word.** The pair is "not really a valid overloading. We want to say that the type variable I extends a type, say, Index which either excludes Range[I] or is a supertype of Range[I]. However, we cannot say that because ... `a[1, 2, 3]` ... the arguments are passed as a tuple ... we need a magic to convert" (`Specification/appendices/future.tex:186-207`, among the team's issues to discuss, 2009).

- **The range beside the trivial range (40 errors) is valid at every fixed `I`.** By the text's instantiation exclusion (`overloading.tex:584-592`), `Range[\I\]` and `TrivialOpenRange` (an `OpenRange[\Any\]`, `fsi:2218`) meet only at `I = Any`, where the trivial one is more specific with the same result. But the text does not say whether a trait's own parameter is fixed by the receiver in this check; the checker ranges it.
